title: Limits of Disclosure in Search Markets
abstract: arXiv:2506.06319v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper examines competitive information disclosure in search markets with a mix of savvy consumers, who search costlessly, and inexperienced consumers, who face positive search costs. Savvy consumers incentivize truthful disclosure; inexperienced consumers, concealment. With both types, equilibrium features partial disclosure, which persists despite intense competition: in large markets, firms always conceal low valuations. Inexperienced consumers may search actively, but only in small markets. While savvy consumers benefit from increased competition, inexperienced consumers may be harmed. Changes in search costs have non-monotone effects: when costs are low, sufficient reductions increase informativeness and welfare; when costs are high, the opposite.

translated_title: 搜索市场中信息披露的极限
translated_abstract: 本文研究了搜索市场中的竞争性信息披露问题，市场中混合存在两类消费者：精通型消费者（搜索无成本）和新手型消费者（面临正的搜索成本）。精通型消费者会激励企业进行真实披露，而新手型消费者则会激励企业隐瞒信息。当两类消费者同时存在时，均衡呈现部分披露的特征，且这种部分披露即使在激烈竞争中依然持续存在：在大型市场中，企业总是会隐瞒低估值信息。新手型消费者可能会进行积极搜索，但仅限于小型市场。尽管精通型消费者从竞争加剧中受益，新手型消费者却可能受到损害。搜索成本的变化具有非单调效应：当成本较低时，足够幅度的成本降低会提高信息性和社会福利；当成本较高时，效果则恰恰相反。
tldr: 在混合存在精通型与新手型消费者的搜索市场中，均衡状态下的部分信息披露在激烈竞争中持续存在（企业总是隐瞒低估值），竞争加剧损害新手型消费者利益，且搜索成本变化对信息性与福利产生非单调影响。
en_tdlr: In search markets with a mix of savvy and inexperienced consumers, partial disclosure persists even under intense competition—with firms always concealing low valuations—while competition harms inexperienced consumers and search cost changes have non-monotone effects on informativeness and welfare.
